findings.issue: The capability description states "unsubscribe link" and dataNeeds includes "unsubscribe token", meaning the email body will contain a clickable URL (e.g. `/widget/unsubscribe?token=xxx`). Clicking a link in an email browser-opens a GET request. The only declared unsubscribe route is `POST /widget/unsubscribe`. There is no `GET /widget/unsubscribe` route in externalContracts. In production, every shopper who clicks the unsubscribe link will receive a 404 or method-not-allowed error — the feature is entirely broken for its primary use path.
findings.fix: Add a `GET /widget/unsubscribe` externalContract (requestShape: {unsubscribe_token: "text"}, responseShape: {success: "flag", message: "text"}) that handles the click from the email body; the existing POST can remain for programmatic use.

findings.issue: The column is declared with `role: "timestamp"` but its `purpose` explicitly states "UTC calendar date (not time)". The spec warns directly about this contradiction: if the coding agent creates a datetime/timestamptz column (the natural interpretation of role `timestamp`), the unique constraint `(item_external_id, item_type, detected_date)` will not deduplicate by calendar day — two webhook deliveries for the same item arriving at different clock times on the same day will both insert successfully, firing a second notification batch and violating the "one notification batch per restock per day" invariant.
findings.fix: Change the column's `role` to `text` (storing the ISO date string, e.g. "2024-11-01") or add explicit guidance in `purpose` that the coding agent must store only the date part (e.g. via DATE type or date-truncation) so the unique constraint actually spans a calendar day rather than an exact instant.
